summary: This lecture continues the story of the Prophet SAW, now an orphan who had lost both parents. After a short quiz on the last episode, the ustaz tells of Abdul Muttalib's love for his grandson, the lost camel, his death and his instruction that Abu Talib look after Muhammad. The Prophet SAW lived with Abu Talib's poor family, but food was enough because of his blessing. At eight or nine he worked as a shepherd, and the ustaz explains five lessons from it: guiding, knowing different characters, courage, a simple life close to nature, and patience. The lecture ends when he is about 12 and wants to go with Abu Talib to Sham.
keyPoints: Abdul Muttalib loved the Prophet SAW dearly, gave him a special seat and would not eat without him.
Before he died, Abdul Muttalib entrusted Muhammad to Abu Talib, who was poor and had five children.
A little food became enough when the Prophet SAW ate with them, and this is barakah.
The Prophet SAW worked as a shepherd for a few cents, and said every prophet had tended sheep.
Shepherding taught him to guide, to know characters, to be brave, to live simply, to be close to nature and to be patient.

chapters.title: Opening and quiz
chapters.summary: After the break the ustaz runs a quiz with sweets as prizes to recall the earlier stories.

chapters.title: A recap of Al-Abwa'
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the place where Aminah died and that Ummu Aiman brought the Prophet SAW back to Mecca.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib's love
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib gave his grandson a special seat, and when a camel went missing he was very worried when the Prophet SAW was late coming back.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib's death and Abu Talib's family
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib died and handed the Prophet SAW to Abu Talib, who had five children.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW grieves but is strengthened
chapters.summary: He became quiet from losing those he loved, and this was Allah's way of strengthening his soul.

chapters.title: The Prophet's manners at meals
chapters.summary: Unlike the other children who scrambled, he was calm, polite and waited his turn.

chapters.title: Blessing in Abu Talib's house
chapters.summary: Though they were poor, the little food became enough when he ate with them, and the ustaz explains what barakah means.

chapters.title: Becoming a shepherd
chapters.summary: At eight or nine he worked as a shepherd, and said that every prophet had tended sheep.

chapters.title: The first and second lessons
chapters.summary: Shepherding taught him to guide the weak and to know the different characters of the sheep.

chapters.title: The third to fifth lessons
chapters.summary: Shepherding trained courage, a simple life and closeness to nature.

chapters.title: The sixth lesson: patience
chapters.summary: The ustaz adds that he learned patience with different characters.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW wants to go to Sham
chapters.summary: At nearly 12 he wanted to go with Abu Talib to Sham, and Abu Talib finally agreed.

dalil.translation: Allah did not send a prophet except that he was a shepherd of sheep. The Companions asked, and you too, O Messenger of Allah? He said, yes, I herded sheep for the people of Makkah for a few coins.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates the Prophet's words when the companions asked whether he too had tended sheep.

lessons.title: Loving a grandchild
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib would not eat without his grandson and held him tight when he returned, an example of a grandfather's love.

lessons.title: Good manners at meals
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW did not scramble or raise his voice and waited for others to take first.

lessons.title: Barakah makes a little enough
lessons.body: A little food was enough for everyone when the Prophet SAW ate with them.

lessons.title: No shame in work
lessons.body: Every prophet tended sheep, and the Prophet SAW worked from childhood even for a small wage.

lessons.title: Guiding the weak
lessons.body: Like a shepherd guiding sheep, the Prophet was sent to show the right way.

lessons.title: Knowing different characters
lessons.body: Everyone's temperament differs, and the shepherd learns to know and coax them.

lessons.title: Courage and a simple life
lessons.body: In the desert he learned to face wolves and the night bravely and to live with few belongings.

lessons.title: Staying close to nature
lessons.body: Living close to nature makes the heart ready to see Allah's greatness, so spend less time on screens.

lessons.title: Patience with different characters
lessons.body: Shepherding trained him to be patient with the slow, the noisy and the stubborn.
